item.title: The Genesis Mission: Can the United States’ Bet on AI Revitalize U.S. Science?
item.description: The test of Genesis's success is institutional: whether it strengthens the United States' capacity to coordinate, implement, and sustain focus on grand challenges across its federated research ecosystem.

item.title: Security Challenges in the Caribbean Amid the U.S. Military Deployment
item.description: Senior Associate Evan Ellis describes the intensifying security pressures the Caribbean is facing just as the United States expands its military operations in the region.

item.title: Unveiling the European Union’s Major Economic Security Update: Is a True Geopolitical Commission Emerging?
item.description: On Dec 3, 2025, the European Union issued a more assertive update to its Economic Security Strategy focused on risk and resilience. As one of few major actors with such a strategy, it aims to cut risky foreign dependencies, protect key tech, and build capacity.

item.title: Taking on Cyber Scams: Ideas for Congress
item.description: Nearly three-quarters of Americans have experienced some kind of online scam, but 68 percent of Americans believe the federal government is doing a poor job stopping them. To chart a new path, Congress must deliver real protections for U.S. citizens.

item.title: NVIDIA’s Jensen Huang on Securing American Leadership on AI
item.description: Huang joined CSIS to discuss policies to accelerate U.S. AI innovation, the role of public-private partnerships in building AI infrastructure, how allied collaboration can strengthen national security, and more.

item.title: Operation of the Agreement Between the United States of America, the United Mexican States, and Canada
item.description: The 2026 USMCA review is a defining test for U.S. jobs, supply chains, and technological leadership. Strengthening the agreement is essential to building a “Fortress North America” that protects workers, secures critical industries, and keeps the U.S. competitive.
